id: HWL1 (DRAFT for dev-PC review, robot PC 2026-11-13): latency budget on the real G1 - holdable sustained lateral push vs a delay added to the estimate in the hold decision (manuscript L1, Fig. hw b)
status: registered 2026-11-17 (robot PC) before the first counted push; hashes in CRITERIA_HWL1.sha256
claim: Prop. latency: the holdable set shrinks by exp(-omega L) for any push profile; omega = 3.8 1/s on the G1, so a fixed-shape push's holdable plateau force falls to 0.927 (L = 20 ms) and 0.859 (40 ms) of its value at no added delay.
controller: S21z4 without steps exactly as experiments/recovery_authority/HWL1_config_S21z4.txt (RA_FZMIN 0.1 = R2 default, DEPLOY_GUARD_VEL_NOSTEP=4, DEPLOY_GUARD_TILT=15, DEPLOY_GUARD_EST_NS=0, no --upper) plus RA_EST_DELAY = 0, 0.02 or 0.04. Changed from the draft (S21d) because S21d's in-hold estimate blow-up tripped the no-step guard on held pushes (robot_pc_reports/2026-11-17/s21y); the simulation check was run with S21p, so the predicted ratios come from the pendulum rate, not from an S21z4 simulation. Fresh process per block; FALCON start-up and automatic hand-over; the block starts >= 2 s after '[RUN] feet carry the weight'.

push.direction: lateral only, from one side, at pelvis height with the load-cell stick (the sim L1 ratios are lateral; fore-aft optional later, separate registration)
push.shape: sustained: load-cell (10 ms mean) duration above 50 % of its plateau 0.5 +- 0.15 s; rise 10-90 % < 0.15 s; plateau = median force between the 50 % crossings; released within the push (no follow-through). The UI shows the live force, the elapsed time and a 0.5 s cue.
push.counted: a push counts iff its shape is inside the tolerance and the 3 s before it were quiet (load cell < 2 N, both feet loaded, no guard); decided from the load cell and contact state only, never from an estimate or the outcome. Out-of-shape pushes are logged and repeated.

procedure.levels: L = 0, 20, 40 ms, interleaved in blocks: block order 0-20-40-40-20-0 repeated; a block = up to 4 counted pushes at one level, ended early by a failure (the guard ends the process).
procedure.targets: per level an up-down staircase on the TARGET plateau force: start 35 N, step 5 N until the second reversal, then 3 N; after a hold the target goes up, after a failure down. The operator aims at the target; the analysis uses the measured plateau, not the target.
procedure.amount: per level >= 32 counted pushes and >= 8 reversals; at most 48 counted pushes per level (power 0.83-0.91 at 32 under the stressed assumptions of hwl1_power_sim_stress.py; 0.94-0.98 nominal); two sessions planned (each failure needs a fresh process).

outcome: per counted push, within 3 s of its onset, by hwl1_analyze.py (hashed): failed if a foot load stays < 5 % m g for >= 0.1 s (step or lift; hold-first keeps >= 10 % per foot, so the 15 % rule of closedloop_sync would read holds as lifts), tilt change > 0.35 rad, lowcmd leg kp drops below 1 (DAMP), or the deploy rows leave RUN (any guard: leg |dq| > 4 rad/s, tilt > 15 deg, ...), or the stream ends; otherwise held. Also reported: hold-first entry time relative to the load cell's 25 N and 50 % crossings, pelvis peak displacement.
estimate_of_the_boundary: logistic regression held ~ plateau force with a common slope and one intercept per level (maximum likelihood); F50(L) = the 50 % force. Ratios r20 = F50(20)/F50(0), r40 = F50(40)/F50(0); 95 % CI by a parametric bootstrap (2000). Sensitivity (reported): the mean of the last 6 reversal targets per level.

predictions.L1-a (primary): r40 < 1: the upper bound of the 95 % CI of r40 below 1.
predictions.L1-b: consistency with the pendulum rate: |r20 - 0.927| <= 0.08 and |r40 - 0.859| <= 0.08 (the simulation band, Fig. 2b).
predictions.reported: F50 per level with CI; the measured hold-entry latency per level (expected +20 / +40 ms over L = 0); the step-free hold count per level; the boundary in DCM displacement delta (Prop. latency, from the load-cell profile) as a shape-independent check.

stop_rules: as CRITERIA_HWH1: tilt > 0.35 rad, joint torque > 0.9 limit, QP fallback > 0.2 s, knee > 70 C, state age > 50 ms (SafetyGate DAMP); vibration without a push -> stop the block; operator stop at any time. Pushes above 80 N plateau are not attempted.
analysis: experiments/robust_holdability/hwl1_analyze.py <runs> (hashed in CRITERIA_HWL1.sha256; smoke-tested on the 11-13/11-16 taps, synthetic data and R2_20261117_140319 / g1lc_20261117_140133 relabelled L0: 14 pushes, 13 held, the 66 N one failed (lift, left RUN), all excluded by shape as they were 0.2 s taps). Uses replay_sync.py for the foot loads.
notes: Entry latency on short 25-30 N taps was 45-210 ms after the load cell reached 25 N (the estimate reads ~0.9 of the force and crosses 25 N late); sustained pushes near the boundary (> 30 N) reduce this. If the boundary at L = 0 exceeds what the operator can push safely by hand (~80 N for 0.5 s), switch to a heavier stick handle or reduce the duration to 0.3 s by amendment before any counted push.
simulation check (dev PC, 2026-11-13): Same protocol in simulation before registration: S21d (EMU 1.7x MPC time, estimate drift 3,5), lateral 0.5 s sustained pushes 20-60 N in 5 N steps, 3 seeds, RA_EST_DELAY 0 / 0.02 / 0.04, zero-step hold. F50 (50 % crossing) 37.5 / 33.8 / 32.5 N -> r20 0.900 (prediction 0.927), r40 0.867 (0.859): L1-b holds for this push shape. L = 0 boundary ~37 N (~19 N s), well below the 80 N hand limit; transition < 5 N wide (3/3 -> 0/3). Script experiments/claude_brace/fdata/l1sim.sh. Hardware boundary may be lower (25-30 N); the staircase follows it, no change after the first block. Delay path checked: hold entry +20 / +40 ms, stance estimate ctrl.d6 unchanged.
staircase helper: sim2real/tools/hwl1_stair.py (operator aid only, not part of the analysis): keeps the per-level target and reversals from the operator's h/f entries; the analysis uses the measured plateau.
amendment 1: 2026-11-17, robot PC, before any counted push of round 2. Round 1 (labels hwl1_L<ms>_b<k>, 15:01-15:09; 1 push counted) is a pilot and is not analysed: without steps the hold layer's release hand-over latched ('post' never cleared because the DCM cannot return without a step) one tick after a hold ended in the L20 and L40 blocks, the stance controller then commanded straight knees and flexed hips, and the L40 block ended in a forward fall after the operator stop (robot_pc_reports/2026-11-17/hwl1_pilot; dev replay DEV_TO_ROBOT sec 14). Controller from now on: HWL1_config_S21z7.txt (hashed) = S21z4 + RA_NOSTEP_NOREL=1 RA_POST_TMAX=1.5 RA_POSTHOLD_GRACE=0.4. Staircase start 25 N instead of 35 N (pilot L0: 0.5 s pushes failed at 27.6 / 31.0 N, held at 20-29 N; steps 5 N then 3 N unchanged). Labels hwl1_L<ms>_r2b<k>. Push shape, quiet rule, outcome, amount, block order, analysis (hwl1_analyze.py, unchanged) and predictions unchanged.
amendment 2: 2026-11-17, robot PC, before any counted push (round 2 had no counted push; its blocks are engineering because of the in-hold posture change, robot_pc_reports/2026-11-17/hwl1_r2). Analysis bug fix in hwl1_analyze.py: the load-cell part of the quiet rule used the window [onset - 3 s, onset - 0.02 s]; with onset = 10 ms mean > 8 N, a fast push already exceeds 2 N inside the last 20 ms, so every push with a fast rise failed 'quiet' (round 2: 22 of 22 with the stick off the robot, median -0.9..+0.5 N). Now [onset - 3 s, onset - 0.3 s] < 2 N (QUIET_END = 0.3). The decision uses the load cell only and no outcome; on the round-2 recordings quiet failures 21 -> 1. Everything else unchanged. Counted HWL1 blocks resume only with a controller amendment once the in-hold posture change is fixed.
amendment 3: 2026-11-18, robot PC, before any counted push of round 3. Rounds 1 and 2 are not analysed: round 1 = pilot (amendment 1); round 2 had no counted push and its pushes were FORE-AFT (kinematic CoM excursion -1.7..-3.3 cm along x, the registration is lateral), with a forward fall after a release (robot_pc_reports/2026-11-17/hwl1_r2 CORRECTION). Controller: HWL1_config_S21z18.txt (hashed) = the no-step env sim2real/config/s21z15/nostep.env (S21z7 + RA_POSTHOLD_GRACE=1.5 RA_ARB_UNREC_LOAD=15 RA_FS_U0=0.01,0.005 RA_ANK_LREG=0.05 RA_PLAN_XF_QUIET=3): the hold-first ankle LP's angular-momentum target chattered between the +-5 N m vertices (hip 5-15 Hz power halved with LREG, z11_hold) and the MPC replans stepped the hold target (cross-faded with RA_PLAN_XF_QUIET=3, dev replay). Hardware check of that common env (2026-11-18 z18_step, step env sharing it): lateral 21-60 N short pushes held without a step. Labels hwl1_L<ms>_r3b<k>. Operator procedure made explicit: stick at pelvis height on the robot's SIDE, horizontal, at 90 deg to the robot's heading, one side for the whole round, the push held until the UI cue (0.35-0.65 s), normal release, stick off the robot between pushes; the env of each block is checked (HWL1_config_S21z18.txt) and a block with another env is excluded. Added counting rule (hwl1_analyze.py, hashed): a push counts only if its kinematic CoM excursion (joint angles + IMU, mid-feet frame, max over onset..end+0.2 s against onset-0.2 s) is mainly lateral (|dy| >= |dx|) - decided from kinematics only, not from the estimate or the outcome; tested on 2026-11-17/18 recordings: lateral pushes y +1.3..+2.9 cm (counted by direction), fore-aft pushes x -1.7..-3.3 cm (excluded). Staircase start 25 N (amendment 1), steps 5 / 3 N, quiet window (amendment 2), outcome, amount and predictions unchanged.
amendment 4: 2026-11-18, robot PC, before any counted push of round 3 (block hwl1_L0_r3b1 had 0 counted pushes: rise 0.16-0.36 s, durations 0.65-5.5 s, pre-push stick contact 2.0-2.6 N; it ended on 'MPC plan expired' after an MPC solve-time jump 10 -> 55-73 ms at t > 90 s, reported to the dev PC). Operator request: no target staircase. Procedure from now on: in every block the operator pushes from weak to strong (start ~20 N, increase by roughly 5 N, varied freely) until a push fails (failure ends the block, as before); the next block of the same level starts again weak. The operator does not look at the outcome to choose the next force beyond 'held -> push harder'. Block order 0-20-40-40-20-0 (interleaved), amount (>= 32 counted pushes per level, <= 48), shape / quiet / direction rules, outcome and analysis (hwl1_analyze.py: common-slope logistic on the MEASURED plateau, parametric bootstrap) and predictions are unchanged; the reversal-mean boundary is no longer reported (no staircase), and the staircase helper is not used. Noted limitation: an ascending series samples forces below the boundary more densely than a staircase and may carry an order effect within a block; the interleaved block order is kept to balance it across levels.
amendment 5: 2026-11-18 18:41:15 local (wall 1794994875), robot PC. Hand pushes could not meet the registered shape: in the first six round-3 blocks (amendment-4 ascending series, all recorded before this amendment) 2 of 56 pushes counted - 10-90 % rise 0.2-0.9 s (rule < 0.15 s) and durations 0.6-3 s (rule 0.35-0.65 s). Decided on the shape statistics, not on outcomes (the operator's impression that L0 held more is disclosed here). For recordings STARTED after this time: a push counts with a duration of 0.25-1.2 s and a rise < 0.5 s (quiet, direction and outcome rules unchanged). The boundary fit adds a common log(duration / 0.5 s) covariate (same for all levels) and F50 is reported at a 0.5 s push; ratios r20, r40 and the decisions are computed from these F50. The six earlier round-3 blocks keep the registered shape window (2 counted pushes) and are reported separately as well as pooled. Limitation: the wider window mixes push durations; the interleaved block order and the covariate are the controls.
amendment 6: 2026-11-18 evening, robot PC, before the next round-3 block (no recording after the amendment-5 time exists yet; the PRIMARY set is empty). Pre-registered report: experiments/robust_holdability/hwl1_report.py (hashed) fixes every output before the data. Decisions unchanged (L1-a, L1-b from the amendment-5 model on the PRIMARY set = recordings started after wall 1794994875); if a level has no failure or no hold its F50 is reported as a bound and the dependent decision is 'not estimable' (also on quasi-separation, |covariate coef| > 50). EARLY (round 3 before amendment 5) and POOLED sets are reported, never used for a decision. Secondary analyses, reported without thresholds: S1 hold-entry latency after the 25 N crossing per level (manipulation check, expected +20/+40 ms); S2 per-level counts, held/failed force ranges, failure modes; S3 boundary in impulse; S4 boundary in the LIPM open-loop DCM shift (CoP fixed, omega 3.8) vs exp(-omega L); S5 left/right side intercept; S6 block-within-level and push-within-block covariates (order sensitivity of the ascending series, amendment 4); S7 subset meeting the registered shape window; S8 release rebound (CoM travel back toward the pusher within 1.5 s, held pushes); S9 figure; S10 manuscript macros written to the report folder only. hwl1_analyze.py adds per-push output fields (impulse, delta_dcm, side, rebound, shape_registered, block) - counting rules, outcome and fit unchanged. Procedure reminder (amendment 4): every block ascends until a push FAILS; a level without any failure gives no F50 (the L0 blocks must reach failure, ~50-70 N). Side may be either; the side is recorded per push.
amendment 7: 2026-11-18 evening, robot PC, before the next round-3 block (PRIMARY set still empty). Outcome rule fix: in three round-3 blocks a push was followed 1-3 s later by a slow forward near-fall into the harness (pelvis tilt 13.5-14.9 deg, knees straightened 1.1 -> 0.26-0.40 rad) with the controller still in RUN (no deploy guard: tilt 15 deg, leg speed 4 rad/s; estimate and loop guards off in hold), so the push was scored 'held' (tilt rule 0.35 rad). New failure rules inside the 3 s window: pelvis tilt change > 8 deg against the pre-push median, or a knee < 0.6 rad. Thresholds from all 57 round-3 pushes: held pushes tilt rise median 0.9, p95 4.9, max 5.0 deg (excluding the two below), knee minimum p5 0.86 rad; failures and near-falls 9.3-15 deg. Effect on EARLY data (disclosed): hwl1_L40_r3b2 39.9 N (tilt +12.2 deg, knee 0.40) and hwl1_L0_r3b3 44.1 N (tilt +9.3 deg) become failed. Applies to all recordings. Safety (not analysis): no-step blocks run with DEPLOY_GUARD_TILT=10 and the new opt-in DEPLOY_GUARD_KNEE=0.6 (deploy_real.py) so a near-fall ends the run (HOLD -> DAMP); held pushes reached at most 7.8 deg absolute (p95). Everything else unchanged.
amendment 8: 2026-11-18 22:00 local, robot PC: data collection STOPPED after block b16 (3 cycles, PRIMARY set 54 counted pushes: L0 22, L20 15, L40 17; registered amount >= 32 per level NOT reached). Decision by the operator and the robot PC after an interim report (hwl1_report.py on b11-b16, sim2real/robot_pc_reports/2026-11-18/hwl1_r3_round, marked INTERIM) - disclosed: the interim result WAS seen. Reason given is resolution, not direction: with 7 failures scattered over 22-50 N and holds up to 68 N the common-slope fit did not identify a boundary (F50 extrapolated to 260-670 N, ratio CIs 0.05-1.06 and 0.09-5.4), the added delay reached the hold entry only partly (median entry after the 25 N crossing 69 / 78 / 86 ms for +0 / +20 / +40 ms), and the predicted effect (0.93 / 0.86) is small against hand-push variability (shape, direction, stance drift); completing 32 per level was judged unlikely to resolve r40 < 1. Consequences: L1-a and L1-b are NOT tested and NOT reported as met or failed; the manuscript keeps the L1 paragraph off (hwLfalse). What is reported, as pre-specified descriptive outputs of amendment 6 (S1, S2, S10) from the L0 condition only: 21 of 22 counted lateral pushes (load-cell plateau 26-59 N, 0.25-1.2 s) held without a step under amendment-7 outcome rules, hold entry 69 ms (median, IQR 59-144, n 21) after the load cell's 25 N crossing. The post-hoc stance (hip-yaw) covariate mentioned on 11-18 was not computed. No other rule changed.
